The strange area is enclosed by three lines, x=l%%ZSMJ3%%, y=a%%ZSMJ4%% and x=r%%ZSMJ5%%, as its left side, its bottom side and its right side respectively, where l%%ZSMJ6%%, r%%ZSMJ7%% and a%%ZSMJ8%% can be any real numbers satisfying that l<r%%ZSMJ9%%. The upper side of the area is boundless, which you can regard as a line parallel to the x%%ZSMJ10%%-axis at infinity. The following figure shows a strange rectangular area.

A point (xi,yi)%%ZSMJ11%% is in the strange rectangular area if and only if l<xi<r%%ZSMJ12%% and yi>a%%ZSMJ13%%. For example, in the above figure, p1%%ZSMJ14%% is in the area while p2%%ZSMJ15%% is not.

Tokitsukaze wants to know how many different non-empty sets she can obtain by picking all the points in a strange rectangular area, where we think two sets are different if there exists at least one point in one set of them but not in the other.
input: The first line contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ16%% (1≤n≤2×105%%ZSMJ17%%) — the number of points on the plane.
The i%%ZSMJ18%%-th of the next n%%ZSMJ19%% lines contains two integers xi%%ZSMJ20%%, yi%%ZSMJ21%% (1≤xi,yi≤109%%ZSMJ22%%) — the coordinates of the i%%ZSMJ23%%-th point.
output: Print a single integer — the number of different non-empty sets of points she can obtain.
note: For the first example, there is exactly one set having k%%ZSMJ24%% points for k=1,2,3%%ZSMJ25%%, so the total number is 3%%ZSMJ26%%.
